vault.title: Lab 01 - Image basics (numpy)
vault.summary: This document outlines the first laboratory assignment for an Introduction to Computer Vision course, focusing on treating images as NumPy arrays. Students are required to build a 64x64 RGB gradient image, convert it to grayscale, perform array slicing and flipping, compute intensity histograms, and apply thresholding techniques. The final deliverable is a Jupyter notebook named lab01.ipynb containing executable code cells for each task, due by Friday at 23:59 in week 2.
key_terms: NumPy: A library for programming with multi-dimensional arrays in Python.
RGB gradient: An image representation using Red, Green, and Blue color channels.
Grayscale: An image where each pixel represents light intensity, commonly derived using color channel weighting.
Array slicing: A method to extract or manipulate portions of NumPy arrays without loops.
Histogram: A graphical representation of the distribution of numerical data, such as pixel intensities.
Thresholding: A technique used to create binary masks by separating pixels based on an intensity value.

vault.title: CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision Syllabus
vault.summary: This document outlines the 15-week schedule, grading policy, and lab assignments for Introduction to Computer Vision taught by Abenova Saule. Students will learn core computer vision concepts such as image filtering, feature detection, object recognition, and convolutional neural networks. The grading scheme consists of 30 percent labs, 30 percent midterm, and 40 percent final project.
key_terms: Convolution: A mathematical operation used in image filtering.
Edge detection: Identifying boundaries within images using algorithms like Sobel and Canny.
SIFT: Scale-Invariant Feature Transform used for detecting and describing local features.
Homography: A transformation relating the coordinates of points in two images.
RANSAC: An iterative method to estimate mathematical model parameters from data with outliers.
CNN: Convolutional Neural Network used for tasks like image classification.

vault.title: Lecture 01: Introduction
vault.summary: This introductory lecture for CSCI3240 Introduction to Computer Vision covers the course overview, grading policy, and the fundamental concept of representing images as multidimensional arrays using data types like uint8. Students are also introduced to the core software tooling required for the course, including numpy, OpenCV, and matplotlib.
key_terms: Images as arrays: Representation of images using height, width, and color channels.
dtype uint8: Unsigned 8-bit integer data type commonly used for pixel values.
numpy: A library for numerical computing in Python.
OpenCV: A library specialized in computer vision tasks.
matplotlib: A plotting library used for data visualization.
